input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds Customer (Meridian) with an undefined-scope, all-territory non-compete extending 24 months past termination — beyond the walk-away threshold (post-term non-compete over 12 months / undefined "competes with Vendor" scope). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Preferred position is no field-of-use or non-compete restriction on Customer, so § 12.4 is struck; the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, 12 months, carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 12.4: we cannot accept any restriction on the products or services we may develop, buy, or sell, and a 24-month post-term non-compete in any territory also directly contradicts § 12.3. If Copperleaf needs protection for a specific offering, we could consider a narrow restriction tied to one named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month post-term non-compete binding Customer in § 12.4.
